result.title: Train What You Run: Probabilistic Convolutions for Learning Token Compaction in State Space Models
result.summary: Visual token compaction reduces inference cost by passing only selected image patches or video tokens to later layers. In sequence models with local convolutions, each removal changes which tokens are neighbors. Learning which tokens to keep therefore requires a training signal that accounts for the new neighborhoods. We introduce ProbConv, which computes the exact expected convolution before activation at a kept position under independent keep decisions. The operator is differentiable in the keep probabilities. With binary decisions, ProbConv and step gating reproduce the compacted Mamba block. Across image, vision--language and video backbones, ProbConv is strongest under strong compaction: its advantage over matched training controls grows as more tokens are removed. In Cobra, it also outperforms adaptations of published vision--language pruning methods at matched inference budgets. ProbConv also improves over matched zero-mask training in video frame selection and speech frame dropping. Our code is available at: https://github.com/gmum/probconv

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ProbConv：在独立保留概率假设下，精确计算被保留位置在激活前的期望卷积，使 token 保留决策可微；在图像、视觉-语言和视频骨干上验证强压缩时优势随删减比例增大。
AI.relevance_reason: 可微保留概率与「删 token 后邻域改变」的建模，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与动态计算预算提供训练线索，但其目标是推理效率而非 latent 推理状态，实际对推理行为的影响仍待核查。
